title.en: Tell the story at the reunion
title.es: Contar la anécdota en la reunión familiar

es: Contar una anécdota familiar completa (hábito, escena, hecho, giro y desenlace) con secuencia de tiempos precisa y responder con naturalidad a las preguntas del público.

vocabulary.es: salir el tiro por la culata

teaching.en: At every family reunion, my uncle would hold his audience with the same story, while the distant relatives pretended never to have heard it.
teaching.es: En cada reunión familiar, mi tío tenía cautivo a su público con la misma historia, mientras los parientes lejanos fingían no haberla oído nunca.
teaching.explanationEs: Would + verbo base abre la anécdota con un hábito del pasado; aquí una acción que se repetía.
segments: At every family reunion, my uncle would hold his audience with the
same story, while the distant relatives pretended never to have heard it.
teaching.audioText: At every family reunion, my uncle would hold his audience with the same story, while the distant relatives pretended never to have heard it.

teaching.en: My grandmother had been planning for weeks to play a prank on the whole family, and nobody suspected a thing.
teaching.es: Mi abuela llevaba semanas planeando gastarle una broma a toda la familia, y nadie sospechaba nada.
teaching.explanationEs: Had been planning: una actividad en curso antes del momento que se cuenta; da el giro.
segments: My grandmother had been planning for weeks to play a
prank on the whole family, and nobody suspected a thing.
teaching.audioText: My grandmother had been planning for weeks to play a prank on the whole family, and nobody suspected a thing.

teaching.en: Just as I was about to blow out the candles, the punchline of her joke arrived: the cake was made of bread.
teaching.es: Justo cuando iba a soplar las velas, llegó el remate de su broma: el pastel estaba hecho de pan.
teaching.explanationEs: Was about to + verbo se interrumpe con un hecho; el hecho que rompe la escena llega en past simple.

punchline of her joke arrived: the cake was made of bread.
teaching.audioText: Just as I was about to blow out the candles, the punchline of her joke arrived: the cake was made of bread.

teaching.en: Good storytellers tend to embellish, and it is easy to get carried away, so keep only the details that serve the story.
teaching.es: Los buenos narradores tienden a adornar, y es fácil dejarse llevar, así que conserva solo los detalles que sirven a la historia.
teaching.explanationEs: Embellish es adornar un relato; get carried away, pasarse de la raya por entusiasmo.
segments: Good storytellers tend to embellish, and it is easy to get
carried away, so keep only the details that serve the story.
teaching.audioText: Good storytellers tend to embellish, and it is easy to get carried away, so keep only the details that serve the story.

teaching.en: If the prank were to backfire, the whole family would be ready to see the funny side, as they always were.
teaching.es: Si la broma saliera mal, toda la familia estaría dispuesta a verle el lado gracioso, como siempre.
teaching.explanationEs: If + were to + verbo base plantea una hipótesis poco probable; la familia reaccionaría con humor.
segments: If the prank were to backfire, the whole family would be
ready to see the funny side, as they always were.
teaching.audioText: If the prank were to backfire, the whole family would be ready to see the funny side, as they always were.

teaching.en: When the story ended, the whole audience would burst out laughing, and someone always asked, “Did you really eat it all?”
teaching.es: Cuando la historia terminaba, todo el público se echaba a reír, y alguien siempre preguntaba: «¿De verdad te lo comiste todo?»
teaching.explanationEs: Las preguntas del público usan did + verbo base: Did you really eat…? Responde con una frase corta.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase muestra que la broma se preparó mucho antes de la escena?

choices.text: Little did we know that my grandmother was planning the prank for weeks.
Little did we know that my grandmother planned the prank for weeks.
Little did we know that my grandmother had been planning the prank for weeks.
Little did we know that my grandmother has been planning the prank for weeks.

feedback.es: Had been planning sitúa una actividad en curso antes del momento que se cuenta; was planning, planned y has been planning no marcan esa anterioridad.

hint.es: Busca el past perfect continuous: lo que duraba antes del giro.

origin.text: Ana is telling the story of her grandmother's prank. She wants the audience to understand that the preparations began long before the cake reached the table, and she must choose the right tense for that earlier background.

prompt.es: Completa: «Iba a soplar las velas cuando se apagaron las luces.»

feedback.es: Blow out the candles es la colocación para soplar las velas; was about to va seguido del verbo en forma base.

hint.es: Verbo base que se usa con las velas de un pastel.

origin.text: Everybody was singing, and I was about to ___ out the candles when the lights went off and somebody laughed in the dark.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cuando terminó la historia, todos se echaron a reír.»

answer.text: When the story ended, everyone burst out laughing
accepted: When the story ended, everyone burst out laughing
Everyone burst out laughing when the story ended

feedback.es: El hecho principal va en past simple (ended, burst); burst out laughing se mantiene junto como expresión fija.

hint.es: La cláusula temporal va primero; burst out laughing al final.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué revela la reacción del público.

choices.text: They are bored and hope that he will finish soon.
They are hearing the story for the very first time.
They dislike the way he embellishes the story.
They know the story well but still enjoy hearing it.

feedback.es: Suspiran porque ya la conocen, pero nadie se marcha y hasta los parientes lejanos terminan llorando de risa: disfrutan de la costumbre.

origin.audio: My uncle cleared his throat, and the whole table fell silent. “At every reunion,” he began, “I promise myself not to tell this story. And every year, I get carried away.” The audience sighed, because they had heard it many times, and yet nobody left the table. By the punchline, even the distant relatives were crying with laughter.

prompt.es: Completa: «Pasamos semanas planeando la broma y nadie sospechaba nada.»

feedback.es: Spend weeks + -ing es la estructura natural; planning es la colocación más habitual con prank, y preparing también es posible.

origin.text: It was my cousin's idea, and we spent weeks ___ the prank in secret, although nobody in the house suspected a thing.

prompt.es: Cuenta la anécdota (unas 170 palabras) y responde a las dos preguntas del público.

answer.text:
Every summer, the whole family used to meet at my grandmother's house. The kitchen smelled of coffee, and the relatives were all talking at once. My aunt Mia would always tell the same story about the day she lost her umbrella at the station. That year, she was about to start it again when a stranger walked into the garden, holding an old umbrella. Nobody recognised him. Silence. Then my aunt stood up and put her hand to her face. “It's mine,” she whispered. He had been looking for her for thirty years, and he had kept the umbrella in his house all that time. Little did we know that he would stay for dinner, and that he would become part of the family.
Did you recognise him? No, I didn't. I thought he was a neighbour.
What did your aunt say? Fair enough, she said. Tonight, for once, we will hear a new story.
accepted:
Every summer, the whole family used to meet at my grandmother's house. The kitchen smelled of coffee, and the relatives were all talking at once. My aunt Mia would always tell the same story about the day she lost her umbrella at the station. That year, she was about to start it again when a stranger walked into the garden, holding an old umbrella. Nobody recognised him. Silence. Then my aunt stood up and put her hand to her face. “It's mine,” she whispered. He had been looking for her for thirty years, and he had kept the umbrella in his house all that time. Little did we know that he would stay for dinner, and that he would become part of the family.
Did you recognise him? No, I didn't. I thought he was a neighbour.
What did your aunt say? Fair enough, she said. Tonight, for once, we will hear a new story.

When I was a child, we would all meet at my grandmother's house on Sundays. The kitchen smelled of bread, and the relatives were laughing in the garden. My aunt Mia used to tell the same story about the day she lost her umbrella at the station. One Sunday, she was about to begin when a tall man walked into the garden with an umbrella in his hand. Nobody knew him. Silence. Then my aunt smiled and opened her arms. “That's my umbrella,” she said. He had been searching for her for thirty years, and he had never given up. Little did I know that he would become my uncle's best friend.
Did you recognise him? No, I didn't. I thought he was a friend of my uncle.
What did your aunt say? Honestly, she said nothing. She just hugged him.

feedback.es: Una buena versión abre con hábito o escena, rompe con un hecho o was about to, da el giro con had been o Little did we know y responde a las dos preguntas del público (reconocerlo y qué dijo tu tía) con respuestas cortas.

origin.text: Situación: reunión familiar en casa de tu abuela. Cada verano tu tía Mia contaba la historia del día que perdió su paraguas en la estación. Un año, iba a empezar cuando un desconocido entró en el jardín con un paraguas viejo: era el hombre que lo había encontrado hacía treinta años y llevaba todo ese tiempo buscándola. Cuenta la anécdota (unas 170 palabras) con: un hábito o escena del pasado (used to / would), un hecho con was about to, un giro con had been o Little did we know y un final corto. Después responde a dos preguntas del público: «Did you recognise him?» y «What did your aunt say?».

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere el final sobre la actitud de la familia.

choices.text: That the family cares more about the tradition than about the story itself.
That the family had finally grown tired of the story.
That the uncle was losing his memory and they were worried.
That the cousins secretly preferred a different story.

feedback.es: Nadie lo ayudó porque querían oírlo encontrar el final: lo que valoran es la costumbre de escucharlo, no los detalles de la historia.

origin.audio: Every year, at the family reunion, my uncle Carlos would tell the same story about the night he met my aunt. He would embellish it a little more each time, until the rain became a storm and the walk became a mountain climb. The distant relatives would smile politely, and my cousins would count the new details. Yet nobody ever stopped him. When he reached the punchline, the whole table burst out laughing, even those who could have told it word for word. Last year he forgot the ending. Nobody helped him. For once, we all just wanted to hear him find it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Adorna sus historias: cada vez que las cuenta, el pez crece.»

feedback.es: Embellish es la palabra precisa para adornar un relato; exaggerate y embroider también son posibles, pero embellish subraya el adorno más que la exageración.

origin.text: Every time he tells it, the fish gets bigger. He likes to ___ his stories a little, and nobody minds.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la pausa de Ana en esta conversación?

choices.text: That she has forgotten what happened that night.
That she is exaggerating to keep the audience laughing.
That she is embarrassed about what she ate.
That she does not want to answer his question.

feedback.es: La pausa y «Let's say I got carried away» revelan que adorna la respuesta para divertir; la risa posterior confirma que el público entiende el juego.

origin.text: “Did you really eat it?” asked Leo. “Every bit,” said Ana. “Even the candles?” “Well...” She looked at the ceiling. “Let's say I got carried away.” For a second nobody laughed. Then the whole table burst out laughing, and Leo laughed too.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Toda la mesa se echó a reír al oír el remate.»

answer.text: The whole table burst out laughing at the punchline

feedback.es: Burst out laughing se mantiene junto; at the punchline indica el momento exacto de la reacción.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la postura del autor sobre las historias familiares?

choices.text: That they should be checked against the real facts.
That they reveal more about the family than the event, which is a problem.
That they need not be strictly accurate to be worth telling.
That a good punchline matters more than any other detail.

feedback.es: «Yet that, surely, is the point» defiende que la inexactitud es lo que da sentido a estas historias: no buscan informar, sino reflejar a la familia, y el autor no lo lamenta.

origin.text: Family stories are rarely accurate. Every retelling embellishes them, drops the awkward details and improves the punchline, until the tale says more about the family than about the event. Yet that, surely, is the point: nobody at a reunion wants a report; they want to hear themselves described, a little taller and a little funnier than they were.

prompt.es: Completa: «La broma podría haber salido mal, pero mi tía supo verle el lado gracioso.»

feedback.es: Backfire describe algo que sale al revés de lo previsto; failed no expresa ese efecto contrario y suena menos natural.

origin.text: The prank could easily have ___, but luckily my aunt was able to see the funny side and laughed with everybody else.
